strings.account.logout.message: After signing out, this PC goes offline for this account. The worker service keeps its own sign-in.
strings.login.title: Sign in
strings.login.server.info: Copy the full address from the Server Info page of the admin console. The format is host:port#sha256-fingerprint. The client pins this fingerprint and refuses to connect if the server certificate changes, which prevents man-in-the-middle attacks.
strings.login.totp.title: Two-step verification
strings.login.totp.prompt: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
strings.login.change.title: Set a new password
strings.login.change.prompt: Set your own password before the first sign-in completes.
strings.login.change.info: Your new password is only used locally in the OPAQUE exchange; neither the server nor administrators can learn it. If you forget it, an administrator must reset it and you will need to sign in again on every device.
strings.login.revoked: This device was signed out. Please sign in again
strings.hosts.tags.info: Separate tags with commas. Use the chips above the list to filter by tag.
strings.hosts.delete.title: Delete item
strings.hosts.delete.message: Delete "{0}"? It will be removed on all devices of this account.
strings.hosts.delete.folderMessage: Delete folder "{0}"? Items inside are moved up one level, not deleted.
strings.device.lanOnly: Offline on the server, reachable on the local network
strings.device.selfHint: This is the computer you are using.
strings.device.mobileHint: Mobile devices can control others but cannot be controlled.
strings.device.remove.title: Remove device
strings.device.remove.message: Removing "{0}" signs it out of this account. It will reappear only after signing in on that device again.
strings.cred.privateKey.info: Paste an OpenSSH, PEM or PKCS#8 private key, or import it from a file. Keys and passphrases are end-to-end encrypted before being stored on the server, which never sees them in plain text.
strings.known.delete.title: Delete known host
strings.known.delete.message: The host fingerprint of {0} will be confirmed again on the next connection.
strings.editor.label: Name
strings.ssh.auth.info: Password: saved, or asked on each connection. Private key: uses a key from Credentials. Keyboard-interactive: answer the server's prompts (e.g. a one-time code). SSH agent: not supported yet.
strings.ssh.password.ask: Leave empty to ask every time
strings.ssh.password.info: Saved passwords are end-to-end encrypted and synced to all devices of this account.
strings.ssh.jump.info: If the host lives in the private network of one of your devices and is not reachable directly, pick that device and the connection is forwarded through it.
strings.rdp.jump.info: With a via device, a port forward is set up through it first and the remote desktop app connects to the local port.
strings.rdp.info: RDP hosts open in Windows Remote Desktop Connection (mstsc). Through a device, a local port forward is opened first. A saved password is put into Windows Credential Manager temporarily and removed when the session closes.
strings.rdp.noclient.title: Cannot open Remote Desktop Connection
strings.rdp.noclient.body: Make sure mstsc.exe is available (it works as a client on every Windows edition).
strings.terminal.killed: Session ended on the remote device
strings.terminal.sessions.title: Sessions kept on the remote device
strings.sftp.home.title: Choose a device or host to browse files
strings.sftp.name: Name
strings.sftp.chmod.title: Permissions: {0}
strings.sftp.delete.title: Delete
strings.sftp.delete.irreversible: Deleting on the remote side cannot be undone.
strings.sftp.remoteDirUnsupported: Copying whole folders between two remote sides is not supported yet
strings.remote.noDisplay: No display available on the remote device
strings.ai.mode.info: Read-only: only read operations are allowed. Confirm every step: every state-changing action needs your approval. Confirm dangerous (default): normal actions run automatically; dangerous or unrecognized ones need approval. Full trust: everything runs automatically except the forbidden list, optionally for a limited time.
strings.ai.planFirst.info: The model must first propose a plan; nothing runs until you agree.
strings.ai.composer.placeholder: Message the agent, type @ to reference a device or host
strings.ai.secret.info: What you type is sent by the core directly to the target (into the terminal or input field). It is never sent to the model and never stored in the conversation.
strings.ai.delete.title: Delete chat
strings.ai.unavailable.disabled: AI is not enabled for your account. Ask your administrator to enable it.
strings.ai.unavailable.noModels: Your administrator has not enabled any models for your account yet. Ask them to enable models for you on the Users page of the admin console.
strings.ai.useTarget.title: The agent wants to connect to {0}
strings.ai.pick.noTargets: No devices or SSH hosts in your account yet
strings.ai.pick.noSnippets: No snippets in your vault yet
strings.ai.pick.noForwards: No port forwards in your vault yet
strings.assist.connect.title: Connect with assistance code
strings.assist.connect.info: On an unsigned LemonGalaxy, the other person sees a 9-digit device code and a verification code. The verification code is shown only on their screen and never passes through the server; the session starts only after they click Allow.
strings.assist.request.title: Someone wants to control this Mac
strings.assist.request.info: If you allow, they can see the screen and use the mouse and keyboard. Local security settings are locked during assistance; you can disconnect at any time from the menu bar icon or the banner at the top right.
strings.local.overview.info: This Mac is both a controller and a host. Host settings can only be changed on this Mac; nobody remote, including the server, can change them.
strings.local.perm.missing: Screen Recording or Accessibility is not granted yet, so others cannot see or control the screen.
strings.local.noSessions: Nobody is connected to this Mac
strings.local.accounts.info: Permissions are set per signed-in account. Terminals, files and commands run as the system user configured here, enforced by macOS.
strings.local.controlOnlyOne.info: The controller app can be signed in to one account at a time, used for both controlling and being controlled. Install the host-only client if several accounts need to control this Mac.
strings.local.perm.aiCap.info: The highest mode an AI agent of this account can use on this Mac, regardless of what the controller selects.
strings.local.systemUser.info: The macOS user that terminals, file operations and commands of this account run as.
strings.local.assist.info: Get help without signing in: tell the helper the device code and verification code, they enter them in their LemonGalaxy, and the session starts once you allow it. The verification code is generated locally and the server never sees it.
strings.local.assist.custom.info: 8 to 16 characters. Cannot be changed while assistance is in progress.
strings.local.events.info: Every connection, file operation and command is logged on this Mac; actions started by AI are marked separately.
strings.local.perm.info: Being controlled needs two macOS permissions that only you can grant in System Settings. This page updates automatically once granted.
strings.local.perm.screen.info: Lets others see this Mac's screen; also used for AI screenshots.
strings.local.perm.accessibility.info: Lets others use the mouse and keyboard; also used by AI to read the UI tree.
strings.snippet.info: Snippets are end-to-end encrypted and synced to all devices. Use the snippet button in a terminal's header to insert them.
strings.account.changePassword.info: Changing your password does not sign out other devices; account keys stay the same.
strings.account.totp.info: When on, signing in also needs the 6-digit code from an authenticator app. Your administrator may require it.
strings.account.totp.scan: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app or enter the key manually, then type the 6-digit code it shows.
strings.account.totp.unsupported: The current core does not provide self-service two-step verification yet
strings.settings.language.info: The interface language changes immediately. To add a language, put a language file in Resources\Locales in the program folder.
strings.settings.terminal.theme.info: Color schemes are JSON files in Resources\TerminalThemes in the program folder; add a file to add a theme. Each SSH host can override the scheme in its editor.
strings.settings.terminal.optionMeta.info: When on, Option combinations send an Esc prefix (needed by emacs and bash shortcuts). When off, Option types special characters.
strings.settings.connection.display.info: Actual quality also adapts to the network. Frame rates the host hardware cannot reach fall back to the highest available.
strings.settings.connection.h265.info: Lower bitrate at the same quality. Falls back to H.264 when the host hardware lacks support.
strings.settings.connection.reattach.info: Terminal sessions stay alive on the host after a disconnect. When some are kept, you are asked whether to re-attach or start a new one.
strings.about.mock.info: The built-in mock core (fake devices, files and AI) is in use for demos and self-tests; it is used with --mock or LEMONGALAXY_MOCK=1. Normally the Rust core in galaxy_ffi.dll next to the app is used.
strings.settings.autoHideList: Collapse the list while a session tab is open
strings.settings.autoHideList.info: Terminal, file, desktop and AI tabs get more room; the list comes back when you return to the home tab.
strings.ssh.unsupported: SSH direct connections are not supported by the current core yet
strings.local.account.active: Signed in; used for this Mac
strings.local.account.needsRelogin: Reset by the administrator; sign in again
strings.local.perm.notify.info: Show a banner with a disconnect button at the top right while someone is connected or AI is operating.
strings.remote.closed: The remote side stopped sharing the screen
strings.about.mock.fallback: The Rust core was not loaded ({0}), so the mock core is used: devices, files and AI are demo data. Put galaxy_ffi.dll next to LemonGalaxy.exe and restart to use the real core.
strings.ai.mode.effective: Effective mode (the strictest of your choice, the admin limit and the device owner's limit)
strings.device.selfHint.win: This is the computer you are using. Remote access to it is handled by the LemonGalaxy worker service; see Local access.
strings.editor.unsavedClose: The file has unsaved changes. Save before closing?
strings.local.win.info: On Windows, remote access is handled by lemon-galaxy-worker.exe shipped next to this app. It runs as a system service (LemonGalaxyWorker) that starts with Windows and signs in with the same account as this app. It stays reachable on the lock screen, the sign-in screen and UAC secure desktops; terminals, files and commands run as the Windows user configured for the account.
strings.local.win.disable.message: The LemonGalaxyWorker service will be removed (administrator rights required). Nobody can access this computer remotely afterwards. The account sign-in is kept.
strings.local.win.enableTitle: Allow remote access to this computer
strings.local.win.enableHint: A console window opens as administrator: it signs the worker in with the current server and account (type your password there), then installs the system service.
strings.local.win.enabledHint: The worker service starts with Windows and restarts on failure, even when this window is closed.
strings.local.win.noWorker: lemon-galaxy-worker.exe is missing from the program folder, so remote access cannot be enabled. Please use the full release package.
strings.local.win.commands.info: You can also run these commands yourself in an administrator PowerShell in the program folder.
strings.local.win.f.display: DXGI desktop duplication (GDI fallback), H.264 encoding, keyboard, mouse and clipboard.
strings.local.win.f.lock.info: The lock screen, sign-in screen and UAC secure desktop can be seen and controlled.
strings.local.win.f.terminal: PowerShell / cmd via ConPTY on Windows 10 1809 and later.
strings.local.win.f.files: Paths look like /C:/Users/x; "/" lists the drives.
strings.local.win.f.account.info: The worker uses the same account as this app; it appears in your device list.
strings.local.win.f.ai: AI actions are limited by local caps and the forbidden list; the worker has the final say.
strings.remote.privacy: Privacy screen (black out the remote display and lock its local input)
strings.remote.sound: Sound (play the remote device's audio here)
strings.remote.sound.failed: Could not play the remote sound: {0}
strings.settings.connection.h264only: The Windows client decodes H.264 in software, so H.264 is used even if the remote supports H.265.
strings.settings.terminal.rightClickPaste.info: When on, right-click copies the selection or pastes when nothing is selected (like the Windows console). When off, right-click opens a menu.
strings.settings.terminal.shortcuts: Copy Ctrl+Shift+C, paste Ctrl+Shift+V or Shift+Insert, scroll history with Shift+PageUp / PageDown or the mouse wheel.
strings.sftp.delete.recycle: Local files are moved to the Recycle Bin.
strings.ssh.agent.unsupported: SSH agent authentication is not supported by the core yet. Use a password, a private key or keyboard-interactive.
strings.update.title: Software update
strings.update.info: Updates are downloaded from your own LemonGalaxy server. The release signature is verified before download and SHA-256 after. Installing closes the app, replaces its files and reopens it.
strings.update.mockInstall: Updates are not installed with the mock core
strings.ssh.jumpVia.info: If the host lives in the private network of one of your devices and is not reachable directly, pick that device and the connection is forwarded through it. You can also pick another SSH host as a jump host (up to 3 hops).
strings.hostkey.new.title: First connection to this host
strings.hostkey.new.message: No host key has been recorded for {0} yet. Check that the fingerprint below matches the server. Once trusted it is saved to the vault and checked on every later connection.
strings.hostkey.changed.title: Host key has changed
strings.hostkey.changed.message: The host key of {0} does not match the one recorded in the vault. The server may have been reinstalled or rekeyed, or someone may be impersonating it.
strings.hostkey.changed.hint: Do not continue unless you know this change is expected.
strings.hostkey.info: Host keys are stored as known hosts in your vault and shared across your devices. View or delete them under Hosts → Known hosts.
strings.wake.info: This computer (when it is on the same network) or an online device on the same network sends a Wake-on-LAN packet. The target needs Wake-on-LAN enabled in its BIOS or network adapter settings, and must stay powered and connected by cable.
strings.remote.record.savedParts: Recording saved as {0} files ({1}; the remote resolution changed)
strings.remote.record.empty: The recording was too short; nothing was saved
strings.remote.record.missing: The recording file was moved or deleted
strings.remote.clipboard.info: When on, the clipboards on both computers stay in sync. Text syncs as soon as you copy it. Files and folders you copy on this PC are sent to the remote computer; once you see “Copied to the remote clipboard”, paste them there. Files copied on the remote computer are downloaded when you move the pointer back over the remote screen; paste them in File Explorer when it finishes. Up to 4 GB or 10,000 files at a time; use Files for anything larger. Copying files needs clipboard and file access on the remote computer.
strings.remote.files.pushingMany: Copying {0} files to the remote computer
strings.remote.files.pullingMany: Copying {0} files from the remote computer
strings.remote.files.pushed: Copied to the remote clipboard. Paste it on the remote computer.
strings.remote.files.pulled: Copied to this PC’s clipboard. Paste it in File Explorer.
strings.remote.files.noPermission: The remote computer has not granted clipboard and file access, so files cannot be copied.
strings.remote.files.localFailed: Could not write to this PC’s clipboard
strings.forward.delete.title: Delete port forward
strings.forward.delete.message: Delete “{0}”? It is stopped first if running, and removed from your other devices too.
strings.forward.info: Maps a TCP port that the device or SSH host can reach to 127.0.0.1 on this computer, so local database clients, browsers or remote desktop apps can connect to the local address. Rules are stored in your end-to-end encrypted vault and shared across your devices; whether a rule runs is up to each computer.
strings.forward.autoStart.info: Starts this forward after you sign in and stops it when you sign out. If you stop it by hand it stays stopped until the next sign-in.
strings.forward.local.info: Leave empty or enter 0 to pick a free port each time it starts; the actual port is shown in the list.
strings.forward.target.info: The address as seen from the device or SSH host; 127.0.0.1 is that machine itself.
strings.forward.via.choose: Choose a device or SSH host
strings.forward.via.info: Through a device the traffic goes over the end-to-end encrypted session and the owner must allow port forwarding. Through an SSH host it works like ssh -L; you are asked for passwords or to confirm the host key when needed.
strings.local.win.lockOnEnd.info: Locks this computer 10 seconds after all sessions that viewed the desktop have ended; reconnecting after a dropped connection does not count as ending. Changing it asks for administrator rights; the switch shows the value last set from this computer.
strings.local.win.lockOnEnd.on: Lock after remote sessions end is on
strings.local.win.lockOnEnd.off: Lock after remote sessions end is off
strings.local.win.lockOnEnd.failed: Could not change the setting (exit code {0})
